items.title: 12.2.3 Synthesis of ammonia from ammonium salts

source_refs.note: Topic 12.2.3 with Figure 12.3, printed page 275. The printed product 'NaCl' is read as calcium chloride and noted.

blocks.text: In the laboratory ammonia gas is made by heating an ammonium salt such as ammonium chloride with a base such as calcium hydroxide (Figure 12.3): 2NH4Cl(s) + Ca(OH)2 gives CaCl2 + 2H2O(l) + 2NH3(g). In this acid-base reaction NH4+ acts as an acid by donating H+ and OH- as a base by accepting it; the reaction displaces ammonia gas from the ammonium salt and leaves a salt and water. It is commonly used to identify ammonium in salt analysis: a gas with a pungent smell that turns moist red litmus paper blue indicates ammonium in the compound.

blocks.alt: Laboratory set-up. A boiling tube holding a white solid mixture is clamped to a stand and heated at its closed end by a burner; its mouth slopes slightly down and is closed by a cork. A delivery tube runs to the foot of a drying tower packed with white lumps. A tube from the top of the tower enters an inverted gas jar held by a second stand; arrows at the mouth of the jar show air escaping. Pointer arrows mark the mixture, the lumps and the jar.
